evidence: paper: \Delta v = -c_{i_0}^{-1} N_{i_0}^{-1} E_\theta^{\circ}, \qquad \gamma_d = -c_{i_0}^{-1} N_{i_0}^{-1} E_z^{\circ}, \qquad \Psi_* = T_1 \gamma_d, \qquad \Delta\beta = -\varepsilon \partial_Z \Psi_*, \qquad \Delta\gamma = (D_r + R^{-1})\Psi_*

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same five definitions, with the Y-centering folded into the operator. The paper writes -c_{i0}^{-1} N_{i0}^{-1} applied to the already-centred E^o; the Lean's temporalAtIndex applies TemporalMeanUpdate.centered itself and then temporalInverse (= N_{i0}^{-1}, characterised by temporalInverse_solves: graphDz (temporalInverse f) = f) with prefactor -(Tg^{i0} Q_n^{1+h})^{-1}, which is the paper's c_{i0}^{-1} = Q^{-1-h} Tg^{-i0} (p. 110, same page). Delta v is the angular component and gamma_d the axial source, both instances of temporalAtIndex applied to the theta- and z-residuals. Psi_* = T_1 gamma_d is streamPotential, whose docstring gives the same formula r^{-1} Ic(r gamma_d) that the paper's T_1 denotes. Delta beta and Delta gamma are streamBeta/streamGamma verbatim, with D_r = graphDr and R^{-1} = divideRadius. I matched the operators by their definitions, not by re-deriving T_1's mapping properties.
